scenes.heading: Expanding binomial products
scenes.say: What happens when you multiply one bracket by another bracket? In this video you will learn to expand binomial products, step by step.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Every player shakes hands with every player in the other team
scenes.science: Every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other
scenes.breaks: Handshakes have no signs, but terms do: each term carries its plus or minus into every product.
scenes.say: Picture two teams of two players. Every player shakes hands with every player in the other team, so there are four handshakes. Expanding two brackets is the same: each term in the first bracket multiplies each term in the second, so you always get four products.

scenes.heading: The rule
scenes.equation: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd
scenes.say: Here is the rule. a plus b, times c plus d, equals a c plus a d plus b c plus b d. FOIL helps you remember: firsts, outers, inners and lasts.

scenes.heading: The area model
scenes.say: Here is a rectangle with sides x plus four and x plus two. First the four boxes are drawn, then the side lengths, then each box is filled in: x squared, four x, two x and eight. Add them up and the area is x squared plus six x plus eight.
scenes.caption: A rectangle with sides x + 4 and x + 2. The boxes are x², 4x, 2x and 8. Add them up: the area is x² + 6x + 8.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Expand (3x − 4)(2x − 5).
scenes.say: Expand three x minus four, times two x minus five. Firsts give six x squared. Outers give negative fifteen x. Inners give negative eight x. Lasts: negative four times negative five is positive twenty. Collect the middle terms: six x squared minus twenty-three x plus twenty.
scenes.caption: Expand (3x − 4)(2x − 5). Firsts: 6x². Outers: −15x. Inners: −8x. Lasts: −4 × −5 = +20. Collect: 6x² − 23x + 20.

scenes.heading: Watch out
scenes.say: The most common mistake is multiplying only the firsts and the lasts. x plus five times x plus three is not x squared plus fifteen. You need all four products, so the answer is x squared plus eight x plus fifteen.
scenes.caption: The most common mistake is multiplying only the firsts and lasts. (x + 5)(x + 3) is not x² + 15. You need all four products: x² + 8x + 15.

points: Keep each sign with its term
Collect like terms, then check with x = 1
scenes.say: Quick recap. Two binomials give four products. Use FOIL or an area grid. Keep each sign with its term, collect like terms, and check by putting x equals one into both. Now try the practice questions!
